newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Frei heads to Canada to sign trade deal.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Frei heads to Canada to sign trade deal.

text.p: President Eduardo Frei leaves for Canada on Saturday to sign Chile's latest free trade deal and will later travel to the Philippines for an Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.
Frei, presiding over Latin America's fastest-growing economy, and Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien were due to give the official stamp to their bilateral free trade accord in Ottawa on Monday.

The agreement, which will slash trade barriers between the countries, won't actually take effect until after it's been translated into Spanish, English and French and approved by both countries' legislatures, Chilean officials said.
When it does, it will erase tariffs immediately on 80 percent of trade between the countries and phase out almost all the rest over 18 years.

The deal with Canada goes further than other recent agreements because it carries provisions for service industries and environmental and labor clauses like those in the North American Free Trade Agreement, which Chile hopes to join next year or in 1998.

"The agreement with Canada is the widest-ranging that this country has ever signed in the trade area," Frei said in a speech on Friday. He leaves Chile just before midnight (0500 GMT) and arrives in Canada on Sunday.
